name: Frac des Pays de la Loire
funding: State through DRAC Pays de la Loire and Région Pays de la Loire. Main patron Fondation Sodebo since 2012; Collection RAJA backed the 2024 Veilhan show.
watch: Food and packaging patrons. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Names its main patron Sodebo and a 2024 project patron on its patronage page, and names its president and staff; no reports, accounts or board.

name: Fresh Milk Art Platform
funding: Mellon Foundation unrestricted grant of US$350,000 over 2024 to 2026, plus restricted grants of BBD 150,000 in 2024. Runs the FM/CLF fellowship with the Clara Lionel Foundation.
watch: Artist-led platform in Barbados. The 2024 report does not name its restricted-grant donors.
records_note: Posts a 2024 report with financial statements, names funders and its three directors; the accounts are compiled by an accountant, not audited.

name: Friart Kunsthalle Fribourg
funding: Canton of Fribourg, City and Agglomeration of Fribourg, Loterie Romande, Banque Cantonale de Fribourg, the Sandoz family foundation and the Friends association.
watch: Loterie Romande is a public lottery, no flag. Partners include the University of Fribourg and Fribourg Tourisme. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; the about page names backers and partners without a date and lists the association committee.

name: Fries Museum
funding: Provinsje Fryslân gives fixed subsidy; OCW and VriendenLoterij support; Windpark Fryslân is a named partner, with Fonds 21, Mondriaan Fonds, Cultuurfonds, VSBfonds, Turing and Wetterskip Fryslân.
watch: Director Kris Callens left in February 2025; the museum cited transgressive behaviour. ING and ABN AMRO are not on the current partners page.
records_note: The Fries Museum posts annual reports for 2003 to 2024, links full accounts on an ANBI site, names partners undated, and lists its supervisory board.

name: Fruitmarket Gallery
funding: £1.6M. Creative Scotland Regular Funding, City of Edinburgh Council, trusts and patrons.
watch: Dropped Baillie Gifford in 2024 under pressure.
why_flagged: Dropped Baillie Gifford in 2024 under pressure.
records_note: It posts no annual reports, files returns with the Scottish charity regulator, names current supporters without a date, and lists its board.

name: Frye Art Museum
funding: Charles and Emma Frye's bequest runs the museum as a private operating foundation. FY2025 revenue: investment distributions 75.6 percent ($6.9M), donations 16.9 percent, store and events 8.1 percent.
watch: The Art Workers Union picketed on 10 April 2020 and petitioned after the museum laid off 21 part-time workers; the director denied union motives.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2011 to 2025, a named 2025 donor list and its trustees; Form 990 filings run 2001 to 2024 on ProPublica.

name: Fundación Casa de los Tres Mundos
funding: Small cultural foundation built with German, Austrian, Swiss and Dutch government grants and the City of Granada; closed by the Nicaraguan state in 2024.
watch: Founded 1987-89 by Ernesto Cardenal and Dietmar Schönherr. Ran art and music schools and Radio Volcán.
records_note: The foundation's archive site names its 2022 board but posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list; closed in 2024.

name: Fundació Antoni Tàpies
funding: Private foundation with Catalan public support.
records_note: It posts annual reports of activities for 2025 and 2026, audit reports 2015 to 2024, a grants table to 2025 and names its trustees.

name: Fundación Ama Amoedo
funding: Family money traces to Fortabat's Loma Negra cement.
watch: Wealth is inherited from the Fortabat family (cement, an allowed sector). No controversy found.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts or donor list found; the site names the founder-president and staff but no board.

name: Fundación Casa Wabi
funding: Artist-founded non-profit (Bosco Sodi, 2014); 2026 sponsors: Harp Helú, Home Depot, Teka, Grupo Habita, Tequila 1800, Punta Pájaros, Nirox Foundation.
watch: Allowed money named: alcohol (Tequila 1800), retail (Home Depot), hotels/property (Grupo Habita, Punta Pájaros), banking family (Harp Helú).
records_note: Casa Wabi thanks its sponsors with an undated page of logos and lists staff directors, but posts no annual reports, accounts or board.

name: Fundación Oswaldo Vigas
funding: Artist-estate non-profit founded 2010; no funding sources disclosed.
records_note: Its site has a staff page naming a chairman, custodian and director, but no board, reports, accounts or funders.

name: Fundación Sala Mendoza
funding: Founded 1956 by the Mendoza industrial family; partly self-funded through bookstore and art sales.
records_note: Its La Sala page names a president and general manager but no board; there are no reports, accounts or sponsor lists.
